subject: radiology
title: Aortoiliac stenting: forks and inflow

steps.tx: Aortoiliac disease narrows inflow at the fork, so buttock and thigh claudication dominates over calf pain. The patient describes cramps in buttocks and thighs with weak femoral pulses that worsen on exertion daily. A **TASC grade** sorts lesion complexity, and a short focal stenosis suits endovascular treatment first in practice. **Kissing iliac stents** rebuild a diseased bifurcation without open surgery and restore inflow to both legs. Smoking cessation with statins and antiplatelets underpins every revascularisation and protects the result over years.
steps.say: Aortoiliac disease narrows inflow at the fork so buttock and thigh pain dominates over calf pain. The patient describes cramps in buttocks and thighs with weak pulses that worsen on exertion. A formal grade sorts lesion complexity and a short focal narrowing suits endovascular treatment first. Kissing stents rebuild a diseased fork without open surgery and restore inflow to both legs. Smoking cessation with statins and antiplatelets underpins every result and protects patency over years.

steps.tx: Stent choice in the iliac system follows vessel size, tortuosity and the need for precise placement. A **balloon expandable stent** places precisely at an ostium without jumping forward during deployment at the origin. A **self expanding stent** flexes with a tortuous external iliac artery and conforms to changing vessel calibre. A **covered iliac graft** seals an aneurysmal or ruptured segment reliably when bleeding threatens the patient acutely. The **kissing technique** inflates both limbs together and that simultaneity protects the fork from plaque shift.
steps.say: Stent choice in the iliac system follows vessel size and tortuosity and the need for precision. A balloon expanded stent places precisely at an ostium without jumping forward during deployment. A flexible stent conforms to a tortuous external iliac artery and changing vessel calibre there. A covered graft seals an aneurysmal or ruptured segment reliably when bleeding threatens the patient. The kissing method inflates both limbs together and that simultaneity protects the fork from shift.

steps.tx: This frontal angiogram shows the aortic bifurcation rebuilt with stents that extend into both iliac arteries together. The upper segment shows a **balloon expandable stent** at the fork, while the lower segment shows a flexible **nitinol segment** in the iliac limb. Flow continues into a **preserved internal iliac** artery on the left, which protects pelvic perfusion after reconstruction. The image matters for the exam because kissing reconstruction restores inflow without sacrificing every pelvic branch. Precise ostial placement and branch preservation together decide a durable result.

steps.tx: Coverage of an internal iliac artery carries a pelvic price, and the operator weighs that price before deployment. **Internal iliac coverage** risks buttock claudication with erectile dysfunction when both sides lose inflow after treatment. The operator therefore preserves **at least one internal iliac** whenever anatomy allows a safe landing zone. Extensive pelvic coverage rarely threatens the cord, but **spinal ischaemia** remains a vigilance point after long coverage. The team stages limbs in selected patients because staging protects the kidneys from a single large contrast load.

steps.tx: Follow up after iliac stenting proves durability with walking, pressure measurement and duplex together over time. The **ankle brachial index** combined with duplex confirms lasting patency at each surveillance interval after stenting. Returning claudication with **restenosis** earns re ballooning before the stent occludes completely in the iliac segment. Lifelong **antiplatelets with statins** guard the metal, while restarted smoking accelerates failure of the reconstruction. A supervised **exercise programme** extends walking distance beyond metal alone and supports the patient after discharge home.
